headline: AI Character Consistency Across 24 Pages of a Generated Picture Book
summary: Generating a single illustration is easy, but maintaining character identity and style across an entire book presents a unique challenge for AI models.
details: Generating a child's likeness from a reference photo is straightforward for AI, but ensuring that same child remains consistent across 24 distinct pages of a picture book is a significant hurdle.

While individual pages might be plausible, errors in identity and style can compound when viewed sequentially, leading to jarring inconsistencies like a child aging years between pages or a drastic shift in artistic style.

Maintaining identity consistency relies heavily on the reference embedding's weight, especially when the character undergoes changes in pose, expression, or lighting. Style consistency, on the other hand, is more manageable through fixed seeds, identical prompt fragments, and constant sampler settings.

The author emphasizes that the entire book should be regenerated if a single page is flawed, as regenerating only one page will likely create new inconsistencies with its neighbors. This means a single mistake can necessitate a full regeneration.
To combat identity drift, the author suggests weighting identity conditioning higher than might seem necessary, as users are more forgiving of stiff poses than an unrecognizable character.
Constraining the scene vocabulary and palette across all pages can also mask subtle style drifts that might otherwise be noticeable in wildly varying environments.

Standard per-image quality metrics fail to capture this problem, as consistency is a property of the entire set, not individual components. This challenge is mirrored in other AI applications, such as generating consistent cloned voices for audiobooks.

The author's work at StoryMine focuses on solving this problem to produce keepsake books from a single photo, with the same face appearing on every page. While the specific mitigations may evolve with new models, the categories of challenges remain durable.
caption:
AI can generate one perfect image, but can it keep a character consistent across 24 pages of a picture book? The challenge lies in maintaining identity and style.

headline: Enterprise AI agents deployed ahead of governance controls, report finds
summary: Most companies knowingly deployed AI agents without necessary controls, and now plan to upgrade or switch vendors within a year, a new study reveals.
details: Enterprises have knowingly deployed AI agents without adequate governance, according to five parallel surveys by VentureBeat Research. A significant majority of companies (57% to 68%) plan to change vendors or add new ones within the next 12 months to catch up with necessary controls.

The research measured five key control layers: identity, evaluation, cost telemetry, context, and orchestration. Most deployed 'agents' are simple chatbots, with only 10% of enterprises reporting that true multi-step agents form the majority of their deployments.

Autonomy in AI is outpacing trust in its evaluations. Two-thirds of enterprises either allow agents to push code changes to production based on automated evaluations alone or are actively working towards it. However, only 5% fully trust these evaluations, and half of companies experienced a customer-facing failure from an agent that passed internal tests in the past year.

Organizations allowing AI agents to share credentials are more vulnerable. Sixty-nine percent of companies permit credential sharing, leading to a 63.5% rate of security incidents or near-misses, compared to 40.9% where each agent has its own scoped identity.

Most enterprises running their own GPUs report utilization rates of 50% or less. Rigorous tracking of AI compute costs and returns is lacking, with only 44% of companies diligently monitoring these metrics. The focus is shifting from acquiring more hardware to optimizing existing resources.

AI agents frequently provide confident but incorrect answers due to ungoverned data. Fifty-seven percent of enterprises traced such errors to missing or inconsistent business context, including stale definitions or absent documents. Governing data definitions is crucial before scaling agents.

The AI agent market currently lacks entrenched leaders, with built-in tools from major AI platforms serving as the default. Orchestration, in particular, shows high intent to switch, with 68% planning to adopt, add, or replace platforms within a year.
